comparisons.peer_topic: Allowance for credit losses composition and components
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's allowance for credit losses represents management's estimate of expected credit losses over the remaining expected life of its financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet lending-related commitments, comprising the allowance for loan losses, lending-related commitments, and investment securities.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM define the Allowance for Credit Losses (ACLL) as management's estimate of expected credit losses. JPM provides a more granular definition by specifying that the estimate covers financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet lending-related commitments over their remaining expected life, and explicitly lists the three components (loan losses, lending-related commitments, investment securities). C's disclosure is broader, noting the ACLL covers the portfolio and troubled debt restructurings, and uniquely emphasizes that attribution is for analytical purposes only and the allowance is available to absorb probable losses inherent in the overall portfolio.

sentences.text: (11)The ACLL represents management's estimate of expected credit losses in the portfolio and troubled debt restructurings.
Attribution of the allowance is made for analytical purposes only and is available to absorb probable credit losses inherent in the overall portfolio.

The Firm's allowance for credit losses represents management's estimate of expected credit losses over the remaining expected life of the Firm's financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet lending-related commitments.
The allowance for credit losses generally comprises:
• The allowance for loan losses, which covers the Firm's retained loan portfolios (scored and risk-rated),
• The allowance for lending-related commitments, and
• The allowance for credit losses on investment securities.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's allowance for credit losses represents management's estimate of expected credit losses over the remaining expected life of financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet lending-related commitments, generally consisting of the allowance for loan losses, the allowance for lending-related commitments, and the allowance for credit losses on investment securities.
comparisons.comparison: JPM's disclosure in D407 is substantively identical to D553, reaffirming the definition of ACLL as management's estimate of expected credit losses over the remaining expected life. Similar to D553, it details the composition of the allowance into loan losses, lending-related commitments, and investment securities. This mirrors C's focus on the ACLL as an estimate for expected losses, though JPM consistently specifies the 'remaining expected life' and component breakdowns that C omits, while C uniquely highlights the 'analytical purposes' of attribution.

sentences.text: (11)The ACLL represents management's estimate of expected credit losses in the portfolio and troubled debt restructurings.
Attribution of the allowance is made for analytical purposes only and is available to absorb probable credit losses inherent in the overall portfolio.

The Firm's allowance for credit losses represents management's estimate of expected credit losses over the remaining expected life of the Firm's financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet lending-related commitments.
The Firm's allowance for credit losses generally consists of:
• the allowance for loan losses, which covers the Firm's retained loan portfolios (scored and risk-rated) and is presented separately on the Consolidated balance sheets,
• the allowance for lending-related commitments, which is reflected in accounts payable and other liabilities on the Consolidated balance sheets, and
• the allowance for credit losses on investment securities, which is reflected in investment securities on the Consolidated balance sheets.
